Load a Dataset From CSV Files

Source: R/resolve.R
resolve.dataset.csv.Rd

Read plots and their species records from CSV files and encode them for a model: the plot-level columns (coordinates, covariates, categorical covariates, targets) of a header file, one row per plot, and the species records of a species file, one row per record.

Usage

resolve.dataset.csv(
  header,
  species,
  roles = list(),
  targets = list(),
  config = list(),
  schemaSource = NULL,
  vocabs = NULL,
  names = NULL,
  maxEditDistance = 1L
)

Arguments

header

Path to the header CSV file (one row per plot, with the targets).

species

Path to the species CSV file (one row per species record).

roles

Named list mapping column roles:

  • plot_id: Column name for plot ID (default "plot_id")

  • species_id: Column name for species ID (default "species_id")

  • abundance: Column name for abundance (optional)

  • longitude: Column name for longitude (optional)

  • latitude: Column name for latitude (optional)

  • genus: Column name for genus (optional)

  • family: Column name for family (optional)

  • covariates: Vector of covariate column names (optional)

  • categoricals: Vector of categorical covariate column names (optional)

An optional role is unset by omitting it, or by giving it the empty string, which is the spelling to use when a role has to be cleared from a list that already carries it. A non-empty column name the file does not have is an error, so a typo fails loudly, and so is a key outside this list.

targets

Named list of target specifications, the name naming the target. Each is a list of:

  • column: Column name in the header file (default: the target's name)

  • task: "regression" (default) or "classification"

  • transform: "none" (default) or "log1p"

  • num_classes: Number of classes for classification

  • weight: Loss weight (default 1.0)

  • class_mapping: Named integer vector pinning each class label to its code (default: codes fitted from the data, labels in sorted order)

  • missing: "drop" (default) or "mask". What happens to a plot with no label for this target (an empty or NA cell, or a class outside class_mapping). "drop" leaves the plot out of the dataset. "mask" keeps it: the plot trains and is scored on the targets it is labelled for, and this target's loss, scaler and metrics use only its labelled plots. A plot labelled for no target is left out either way.

A key outside this list, two targets with one name, or an unnamed target is an error. A dataset for training needs at least one target; one built to be scored needs none.

config

Named list of dataset configuration options; a field left out takes the RESOLVE engine's default (resolve.default_config("dataset")), and a key outside these fields is an error:

  • species_encoding: "hash", "embed", "sparse", "rank_pool" or "transformer". hash folds each plot's species into a fixed-width vector of hash_dim buckets; embed gives each of the plot's top_k_species ranked species slots a learned embedding; sparse is the plot's full species-by-abundance vector; rank_pool pools learned species, genus and family embeddings over every species the plot records; transformer attends over them.

  • hash_dim: Hash buckets of the hash encoding

  • top_k: Species hashed per plot and fixed genus/family slots

  • top_k_species: Ranked species slots of the embed encoding

  • selection: "top", "bottom", "top_bottom", or "all". Which species of a plot survive its per-plot budget: top_k for the hash encoding, top_k_species for embed (which rejects "all", having a fixed number of ranked slots), and species_budget for rank_pool, transformer and sparse.

  • species_budget: species kept per plot by selection for the rank_pool, transformer and sparse encodings; 0 = no budget, so every species a plot records is encoded and selection has nothing to narrow.

  • representation: "abundance" or "presence_absence". The value each species carries into every encoding: its abundance, or 1 under "presence_absence" (a pooled dataset then reports no cover). The selection still ranks by recorded abundance.

  • aggregation: "abundance" or "count". How the fixed genus/family slots of the hash, sparse and embed encodings rank a plot's taxa: by the summed value of their species, or by how many of the plot's species they hold. rank_pool and transformer pool each species' genus and family embeddings with the species weights, or under "count" with one weight per species.

  • normalization: "raw", "norm", or "log1p": the abundance values as read, scaled to sum to one per plot, or log1p-transformed

  • track_unknown_fraction, track_unknown_count: add the share and the number of a plot's species the vocabulary does not know as columns

  • use_taxonomy: encode the genus/family roles

  • pool_weighting: rank_pool weighting "binary", "abundance", "log1p", "norm", or "rank"

  • pool_species_cap: rank_pool per-plot species cap; 0 = no cap, -x = the (100 - x)th percentile of species per plot, computed on the data loaded (-1 = p99, -5 = p95; x in 1..99), >0 = manual cap

  • missing_values: "indicate" or "zero": a missing covariate or coordinate cell is flagged and filled with the fitting fold's mean, or read as 0

  • zero_abundance_as: the abundance a recorded 0 is read at

schemaSource

Optional ResolveDataset (from a previous resolve.dataset.csv() call). When supplied, this dataset is encoded against that dataset's species / taxonomy / categorical vocabularies and classification class mappings instead of fitting its own, so a held-out or transfer set lines up with the training set's embedding namespaces. Default NULL fits fresh vocabularies.

vocabs

Optional vocabulary list from predictor$vocabs() (or dataset$vocabs()). Same effect as schemaSource, sourced from a CHECKPOINT rather than an in-memory training dataset, so the training CSVs need not exist. This is the path for scoring new data: every non-hash encoder indexes an embedding table with a code that is a function of the file the vocabulary was fitted on, so a dataset built without the training vocabularies looks up the wrong rows and predictor$predict_dataset() rejects it. Pair with config = predictor$dataset_config(). Mutually exclusive with schemaSource. A vocabulary list without a species vocabulary (a checkpoint that stores only the vocabulary sizes) is refused.

names

Resolve the species names against the vocabulary of vocabs (or schemaSource) before encoding: the path of the release's names.json, which maps entered names and synonyms to the names the model learnt, or TRUE for the vocabulary alone. A name is taken as written where the vocabulary holds it, else through the table, else as the nearest known name within maxEditDistance edits; dataset$species_names() then lists the names not found as written, with the route each took. NULL (default) reads every name as written.

maxEditDistance

With names: the edits a misspelled name may be away from a known name (default 1; 0 turns the spelling step off; 2 can also rename species the models never saw).

Value

A ResolveDataset object (an Rcpp module class) with methods:

  • coordinates(): Get coordinate matrix

  • covariates(): Get covariate matrix

  • hash_embedding(): Get hash embedding matrix

  • genus_ids(), family_ids(): Get taxonomy ID matrices

  • targets(): Get target values as named list

  • schema(): Get dataset schema

  • plot_ids(): Get plot IDs

  • n_plots(): Get number of plots

  • species_names(): with names, the names not found as written (a list of name, token, route, source, via, distance, n_records)

Examples

plots <- system.file("extdata", "plots.csv", package = "resolveR")
species <- system.file("extdata", "species.csv", package = "resolveR")
roles <- list(plot_id = "plot_id", species_id = "species", abundance = "cover",
              genus = "genus", family = "family", latitude = "lat", longitude = "lon")
targets <- list(elevation = list(column = "elevation", task = "regression"),
                habitat = list(column = "habitat", task = "classification"))
dataset <- resolve.dataset.csv(
  plots, species, roles = roles, targets = targets,
  config = list(species_encoding = "hash", hash_dim = 64, top_k = 5)
)
dataset$n_plots()
dataset$schema()$n_species
